narrative.human_title: The city where the card became an interface
narrative.why_it_matters: Aquapolis feels like Wizards building a coastal machine out of cardboard. The Pokemon are still there, but the frame has become stranger: H numbers, Dot-Code strips, hidden data, Crystal Type, and secret rows. It is beautiful because it is slightly overbuilt. A collector is not only holding a picture; they are holding the remains of a moment when the card wanted to talk to hardware.

claims.text: The local catalog, Pokemon TCG API, and Bulbapedia identify Vileplume as Aquapolis H31, a Rare Holo Stage 2 Grass Pokemon in the English e-Card Series.

Bulbapedia gives Vileplume's Japanese name as ラフレシア / Ruffresia and connects the Holofoil print to Japanese Wind from the Sea card 004/087, while the non-Holofoil Aquapolis print appears as English 43/147.
The local catalog and Pokemon TCG API record Vileplume H31 with 100 HP, evolvesFrom Gloom, Grass type, Fire weakness, two-Colorless retreat, and attacks Poison Scent and Addictive Pollen.
The local catalog, Pokemon TCG API, and Bulbapedia credit Vileplume H31 to Kyoko Umemoto; the local and API rows also credit Kyoko Umemoto on the non-Holo Aquapolis Vileplume #43 counterpart.

The Pokemon TCG API models Aquapolis as set id ecard2 in the E-Card Series with releaseDate 2003/01/15, printedTotal 147, and total 182; Bulbapedia describes Aquapolis as the English e-Card expansion drawing from The Town on No Map and Wind from the Sea.

Bulbapedia lists Vileplume as H31/H32 in Aquapolis's separate Rare Holo H-number sequence, while the local catalog and API also have a non-Holo Vileplume at #43 with the same Kyoko Umemoto credit, Poison Scent, and Addictive Pollen; agents must keep H31 and #43 separate before comparing images, prices, wants, or seller evidence.

Bulbapedia says Aquapolis used e-Reader-era Dot-Code strips and that some lettered variants carried different strip data; Bulbapedia's Vileplume H31 page records card ID D-56 for the Holofoil print and D-56-# for the Non Holofoil print.

Bulbapedia says the Non Holofoil short strip contains Pokedex information, a brief card summary, and information on the content of the long strip; the Holofoil print carries species, height, and weight data.

Bulbapedia says Vileplume H31's long strip contains map data for the Construction: Action application, and that the English e-Reader Pokedex entry comes from Pokemon Crystal while the Japanese entry comes from Pokemon Gold.

Vileplume H31 matters because Aquapolis turns pollen into control: Poison Scent guarantees a status problem, Addictive Pollen can shut off Supporter cards, and the e-Reader layer makes the flower carry map data for another little application world.

special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify Vileplume / ラフレシア / Ruffresia H31 by the Aquapolis H-number Rare Holo lane: English ecard2-H31 / H31/H32 and Wind from the Sea 004/087 lineage, not the non-Holo #43 / 43/147 sibling.
steps: Confirm English Aquapolis / Pokemon TCG API card id ecard2-H31 / printed number H31 before accepting this as the H-number holo row.

Preserve H31/H32 and Rare Holo as load-bearing identifiers; do not collapse the card into the non-Holo Aquapolis Vileplume #43 row even though #43 shares Kyoko Umemoto, Poison Scent, and Addictive Pollen.
Preserve the Japanese lineage split: Holofoil maps to Wind from the Sea 004/087 while the English non-Holofoil counterpart appears as Aquapolis 43/147.

Use Kyoko Umemoto credit, Stage 2 Grass profile, Gloom evolution line, Fire weakness, two-retreat cost, Poison Scent, Addictive Pollen, D-56 Holofoil e-Reader ID, and D-56-# Non Holofoil e-Reader ID as supporting row evidence, not as substitutes for card number and set identity.
Keep reverse-holo listings, generic Vileplume wants, Grass deck references, and seller-card image claims separate until set, number, rarity, attack text, and image evidence align.

Treat e-Reader, Dot-Code, Flower Pokemon species label, Pokemon Crystal / Gold Pokedex source split, Construction: Action long-strip map data, and application context as identification texture, not proof that a seller's physical card scans, is authentic, or is condition-accurate.

For transaction use, request seller front/back photos, holo surface photos, card-number closeup, and provenance or grading evidence before promoting this catalog identity into any physical-card claim.
